name: ByteDC Data Center (Global Tech Exchange)
developer: ByteDC Solutions Co., Ltd (Cambodia-Singapore joint investment)
notes: Cambodia's first Uptime Institute Tier III Design-certified data center, inaugurated May 2023 at Global Tech Exchange, Land 356 Street R-4, Sangkat Srah Chork, Khan Daun Penh, Phnom Penh. Up to 3 MW IT capacity, PUE <= 1.8, total built-up floor space 81,040 sq ft (7,529 sqm), up to 1,000 IT racks, carrier-neutral colocation, cloud and managed services; joint investment between Cambodia and Singapore (per Knight Frank Cambodia report).

name: Royal Group Elite DC1 / Telcotech Data Center
notes: Telcotech's flagship Phnom Penh colocation facility, Royal Group Elite DC1, earned Uptime Institute Tier III Certification of Design Documents (TCDD), announced 18 July 2025. Carrier-neutral with dual A+B feeds, N+1 UPS, backup generators and precision cooling; scalable from single racks to enterprise suites. Public MW capacity not disclosed. Telcotech is a member of AAG and MCT submarine cable consortia and listed a $20M bond on CSX partly to fund data center infrastructure.

name: Telcotech Kampus data center (Monivong Blvd)
notes: Council for the Development of Cambodia (CDC) approved Telcotech's ~US$27.7 million data centre in the Kampus Building, Monivong Blvd, Sangkat Tonle Bassac, Khan Chamkarmon, Phnom Penh on 18 October 2023 (47 skilled jobs). Telcotech later announced a contract with Kampus to expand its datacenter footprint; Keystone Cable supplied low-voltage cabling as the lease for the Kampus data center was signed. Construction/opening status not independently confirmed in public sources.

name: Chaktomuk Data Center (CDC) PNH1
notes: Chaktomuk Data Center markets itself as Cambodia's first and only Uptime Institute Tier III Plus Design-certified data center, located in central Phnom Penh; PeeringDB lists Chaktomuk Data Center Co. Ltd in Phnom Penh and Uptime Institute's awards list includes Chaktomuk Data Center Co., Ltd. Public MW capacity not disclosed; listed as operational by Baxtel.

name: Kepstar Data Center DC1 (Phnom Penh)
notes: Kepstar Data Centre Management broke ground in November 2022 (during Cambodia Tech Expo CTX 2022) on what it described as Cambodia's first Tier III data centre in Phnom Penh. DC1 is 110,000 sq ft with 6.5 MW critical IT load and 1,600-rack combined program with DC2 (per DCD/Network World). Baxtel lists Kepstar: Phnom Penh as operational, largest facility in the market at ~7 MW; Singtel was reported advising on the projects. MoU signed with Huawei (Cambodia) for data center solutions.

name: Kepstar Data Center DC2 (resilience site ~100 km from Phnom Penh)
notes: Kepstar's second planned carrier-neutral facility: 50,000 sq ft with 3.5 MW critical IT load, reported as a resilience/disaster-recovery site ~100 km from Phnom Penh (per Network World 2022 and World Teleport/Singtel advising report; combined 10 MW and 1,600 racks across DC1+DC2). Exact province of the 100 km-away site is not confirmed in public sources; Baxtel lists Kepstar DC2 as planned. Line is filed under Phnom Penh division per Baxtel's Phnom Penh market listing, with location uncertainty noted.

name: Te Aikhong / Kepstar / Fourtitude Asia JV 'Cambodia's largest data center' (near Phnom Penh)
developer: Te Aikhong Enterprise; Kepstar Data Center; Fourtitude Asia (Malaysia)
notes: June 2018 MOU between Cambodian IT firm Te Aikhong Enterprise, Kepstar Data Center and Malaysia's Fourtitude Asia to build what was claimed to be Cambodia's largest data centre near Phnom Penh at ~US$70 million, with construction to start before end of June 2018 and operations targeted within ~18 months, targeting banks, private companies and government tenants. Later status is unclear in public sources; the project may have evolved into Kepstar's DC1/DC2 program. Listed as planned with 2018 evidence.

name: National Data Center Cambodia (MPTC)
developer: Ministry of Post and Telecommunications (MPTC), Royal Government of Cambodia; Japan grant aid
notes: Government national data center in Phnom Penh: groundbreaking July 2023, estimated completion cost ~$30 million with ~$16 million Japanese grant aid; Minister Chea Vandeth described it as core infrastructure for national digital data storage. Baxtel lists National Data Center Cambodia (Cambodian Ministry of Post and Telecommunications) with ~3 MW and an estimated Q1 2026 launch, as the Phnom Penh market's single facility under construction.

name: Ezecom Data Center (colocation/cloud)
notes: Ezecom, one of Cambodia's largest fibre/telecom providers, operates data center and cloud services in Phnom Penh and is named by Knight Frank Cambodia among the country's leading data centre operators. Public MW capacity not disclosed; site details not published.

name: MekongNet IDC1 and IDC2
developer: MekongNet (Angkor Data Communication Group Co., Ltd)
notes: MekongNet operates two identical Internet Data Center (IDC) facilities at different locations in Phnom Penh (AnAnA Building, 95 Preah Norodom Blvd and SunCity Building, Street 370), each fed by different electricity sources with auto-mode standby gensets; carrier-neutral colocation. IDC1 footprint reported at ~7,072 sq ft (DataCenterJournal). Public MW capacity not disclosed.

name: Seatel Cloud Data Center
notes: Seatel, Cambodia's satellite telecom operator, operates a cloud data center in Phnom Penh; Network World (2022) lists Seatel among Phnom Penh data centre operators and Baxtel records Seatel Cloud Data Center as operational with ~2 MW. Knight Frank also names Seatel among leading operators.

name: Daun Penh Data Center (DPDC)
developer: Daun Penh Data Center Co., Ltd (Daun Penh Group)
notes: Daun Penh Data Center offers colocation, dedicated servers, VPS, cloud servers and web hosting, located on Hun Sen Boulevard, Phnom Penh; a new data center-plus-office facility was designed for Daun Penh Group in 2024 (theroomds) using a modular grid. Baxtel lists DPDC as an operational carrier-neutral facility (extra-small). Public MW capacity not disclosed.

name: HT Networks HTN-IDC
notes: HT Networks Co., Ltd, a Phnom Penh-headquartered network operator, operates its HTN-IDC colocation facility at No. 33-34 St.114, Sangkat Monorom, Khan 7 Makara, Phnom Penh; Network World (2022) lists HT Networks among Phnom Penh data centre operators. Public MW capacity not disclosed.

name: Sinet: Phnom Penh (Sinet Cambodia data center)
notes: Baxtel lists Sinet: Phnom Penh as an operational data center (extra-small, managed-service-provider type) with a reported footprint of ~118,403 sq ft, operated by Sinet Cambodia, one of the country's main ISPs. Limited independent public documentation found beyond directory listings; capacity in MW not disclosed.

name: Metfone / Viettel (Cambodia) IDC and core-network data center
notes: Metfone (Viettel Cambodia), the country's largest mobile operator, maintains core-network/IDC data center infrastructure in Phnom Penh (PeeringDB lists Viettel (Cambodia) Pte. Ltd. in Phnom Penh). Public documentation of a commercial colocation facility and capacity in MW is limited; evidence graded C.

name: FPT Data Center Phnom Penh
notes: Hosting provider Varidata markets dedicated-server locations including an 'FPT Data Center' in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, indicating an FPT-operated facility. No official FPT Cambodia data center page or capacity figures were independently verified in this search; evidence graded C (weak/aggregate).

name: NeocomISP (NTC) data center
notes: Knight Frank Cambodia's December 2024 report names NeocomISP (NTC) among the country's leading data centre operators; Astute Analytica also lists NeocomISP's NTC among the five dominant Cambodia data center colocation players. No public facility details (address, MW) were located in this search; evidence graded C.
